FAQ

Short answers

What is Fresh Terminal?

A terminal you type to in plain words. It answers, and it changes its own pages, menus, layout and look to fit what you do. Every change can be undone.

Do I need to sign up?

No. Open it and type; your stages are saved in this browser. Create an account to get $5 free and cloud save.

Who gets the $5?

First-time sign-ups, once per person.

What does it cost after that?

Model cost plus your markup: 10% by default, and you can set it higher in Settings to support us. The minimum is 5%, so card fees are covered. No account fees.

You buy credits first, in packs of $5, $10 or $25 that refill on their own. Those are coming soon; buying is not wired yet.

What is “your key”?

Your own OpenRouter key. Paste it in Settings; it stays in your browser, calls go straight to OpenRouter, and there is no markup. You are never blocked.

Storage above 100 MB may be metered later, about $0.05 per GB-month (not final, not billed).

Is my data private?

Yes, by default. Signed out, your stages stay in your browser. “Share my data” is off unless you turn it on, and we see an account only if you grant access.

On free usage, each prompt passes through our router on its way to the model; we keep the cost, not your words. Today this is a rule our code keeps, not encryption. Encryption with your own key is coming.

What are stages and tags?

A stage is one workspace: its pages, menu, look and conversation. Click its name to rename it.

Tags are the words it recognises as you type: names, dates, actions. Tap one to change what it means.

Can I undo what it changes?

Yes. Every change is one line with an Undo. Actions lists everything, and Replay (experimental) steps back through a session.

What if I lose my connection?

A prompt you send offline waits on the stage. When you are back, send it, edit it or drop it. Nothing sends by itself.

What is not live yet?

Live sync across devices (the database is published; the app still saves in the browser), multiplayer, voice talk-back (Terminal-talk is an early switch), connectors, teams and self-host, and buying credits.

Is it open?

The source is on GitHub, and FreshStack lists every piece underneath.
